ngram-embedding.d: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's lookup table with 320,001,536 rows × 160 (51.2 B parameters). For each token, 16 rows are fetched by hashing bigrams and trigrams, concatenated into 2,560 dimensions and injected into the 4 residual branches at the layer with index 1, through a context gate and a short dilated conv. It adds capacity at almost no FLOP cost.

ple.d: The name in the code (ple_*) of Qwen3.8's N-gram memory. The acronym is expanded as “position-learning enhancement” (vLLM) or “Per-Layer Embedding” (transformers). Not to be confused with Gemma 3n's per-layer embeddings, which use a different mechanism.

memoria-condicional.d: Capacity stored in a table that is looked up by address, rather than in weights that get multiplied. The cost per token is reading a few rows. It is the “third axis” next to the dense model and MoE (conditional computation).

enderecamento-deterministico.d: The row addresses depend only on the token ids, not on the hidden state. That is why they are known before the forward, and the lookup can be done ahead of time from another memory (CPU, a memory-mapped file).

n-grama.d: A sequence of N consecutive tokens. For position \(t\): bigram \((x_{t-1}, x_t)\) and trigram \((x_{t-2}, x_{t-1}, x_t)\).

hash-multiplicativo.d: A hash in which each id is multiplied by an odd 64-bit constant and the products are combined with XOR: \(h = (x_t m_0) \oplus (x_{t-1} m_1) \oplus \dots\). The final index is \(h \bmod p\) plus an offset.

splitmix64.d: A 64-bit pseudorandom function (it adds \(\gamma = 2^{64}/\varphi\), applies two rounds of xorshift-multiply, with M1 and M2, and a final xorshift) used to generate the PLE hash multipliers from the seed. Deterministic and easy to reproduce bit for bit.

lei-de-zipf.d: In natural language, the frequency of an item falls roughly with the inverse of its rank: a few N-grams are very frequent and the vast majority are rare. This is what makes sharing rows of a hash table acceptable.

hashing-multicabeca.d: Using several independent hash functions (in Qwen: the same \(h\) modulo distinct primes) and concatenating the rows. An N-gram may collide in one head, but almost never with the same neighbor in all of them.

rmsnorm-agrupada.d: RMSNorm applied separately to each group of channels. In the PLE, each group of 2,560 is one residual branch, with gain \(1+w\) and \(\varepsilon\) = rms_norm_eps = 1e-6.

conv-dilatada.d: A 1D convolution that only looks at the past and spaces its taps by \(d\): the output at \(t\) combines \(t, t-d, \dots, t-(k-1)d\). Receptive field of \((k-1)d+1\) positions. In the PLE: \(k=4\), \(d=3\), depthwise over 10,240 channels.

ngram-context.d: The last 2 ids of each request, which the PLE keeps between steps and chunks to build the bigrams and trigrams of the first token of the next batch.

estado-conv.d: The last \((k-1)\cdot d\) inputs of a causal conv, kept per request (plus extra columns for speculative tokens). In the PLE: 9 + 3 columns × 10,240 channels, about 240 KiB per request in BF16.

segmentacao-eos.d: The rule that keeps N-grams from crossing an <|endoftext|>: neighbors from before the boundary (or nonexistent ones) are replaced by the EOS id (248044 in Qwen).

rollback-especulativo.d: During speculative verification, the state of recurrent/conv layers is computed for all candidate tokens and then rolled back to the last accepted one (a shift of num_accepted_tokens − 1).

escala-por-tensor.d: Quantization in which a single scale factor applies to the whole tensor. Qwen's FP8 PLE uses one BF16 scale (weight_scale) for all 320 M rows; dequantization is emb.to(bf16) * weight_scale.

dispatch-quant-method.d: The decision, made by vLLM for each layer, of which QuantizeMethodBase creates the tensors and interprets the bytes. If no method matches, the layer is created in BF16, which for the PLE table means ~102 GB.

mtp.d: Extra modules trained to predict tokens beyond the next one: module \(k\) combines the previous level's state with the embedding of \(x_{t+k}\), goes through a Transformer block and uses the model's head to predict \(x_{t+k+1}\). At inference it becomes a built-in drafter: GLM layer 45 (k=2), Qwen one layer reapplied 3×.

n-predict.d: The number of distinct MTP modules in the checkpoint. vLLM uses this value to decide how to reapply the modules when the number of speculative tokens \(k\) is larger than it.

regra-reuso-mtp.d: In vLLM, if \(k >\) n_predict, \(k\) must be a multiple of n_predict (“MTP module reuse”). With n_predict = 3 in DeepSeek Vision-Exp and \(k \ge 5\) required by the launcher, the smallest valid k is 6 (9, 12… also pass). For DSpark it is only a validation: it drafts the block in one forward, with no cycle. The block-k hotfix exempts it.
